label: Darwall argues that second-personal competence grounds equal standing to hold agents accountable
paraphrase: Darwall's substantive positive proposal: second-personal competence, which qualifies one for accountability, is also sufficient for equal standing as a moral-community member to hold other competent agents morally accountable. Why the requisite competence suffices to confer that standing is a further normative question; it does not automatically establish any particular demand's legitimacy or explain accountability for agents lacking the competence.
